title: Advanced C# Practice Quiz
description: Practice questions covering the Advanced C# topics studied so far.
subject: Advanced C#

questions.question: What is the main purpose of deploying a C# application?

options.text: To make the application available for use in its target environment
To convert every class into an interface
To remove all methods from the application
To guarantee that the application has no bugs

questions.explanation: Deployment makes the application and its required files available in the environment where it will run.

questions.question: Which action is most appropriate when preparing an application for deployment?

options.text: Check the target framework and required dependencies

questions.explanation: The application must be compatible with the target environment and have the dependencies it needs.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of performance optimization?

options.text: To increase the number of classes
To improve efficiency while preserving correct behaviour

questions.explanation: Optimization aims to improve resource usage, execution time, or responsiveness without breaking correctness.

questions.question: Which approach is generally best before optimizing slow code?

options.text: Measure performance and identify the bottleneck

questions.explanation: Measurement helps identify the actual bottleneck so effort is directed at the right part of the program.

questions.question: What is boxing in C#?

options.text: Converting a reference type into an interface
Converting a value type to object or a compatible interface type
Converting a string to an integer
Converting a class into a struct

questions.explanation: Boxing wraps a value type value in an object representation.

questions.question: What is unboxing?

options.text: Extracting a value type from a boxed object
Converting an integer to a string

questions.explanation: Unboxing extracts the value type from a compatible boxed value.

questions.question: What is printed by this code?
questions.explanation: The integer is boxed into an object, and Console.WriteLine prints its value.

questions.question: What happens when this code executes?

options.text: The value is automatically converted to a string

questions.explanation: The object contains a boxed integer, not a string. The explicit cast to string fails at runtime.

questions.question: Which class is designed for efficient repeated modification of strings?
questions.explanation: StringBuilder is useful when repeatedly appending or modifying text.

questions.question: What is printed?
questions.explanation: Append adds the supplied text to the end of the existing contents.

questions.question: Why can repeated string concatenation be inefficient inside a large loop?

options.text: Strings are immutable, so concatenation can create additional string objects
String concatenation always causes a syntax error

questions.explanation: Because strings are immutable, repeated concatenation may allocate many intermediate strings.

questions.question: Which C# type is commonly used to represent a date and time?
questions.explanation: DateTime represents a date and time value.

questions.question: What does this expression calculate?
questions.explanation: Adding seven days to 1 January 2026 produces 8 January 2026.

questions.question: What does DateTime.Parse("2026-10-15") attempt to do?

options.text: Convert the text into a DateTime value
Convert a date into a class

questions.explanation: Parse attempts to interpret a string as a date and time. Invalid or culture-incompatible input can cause a FormatException.

questions.question: What is a C# attribute primarily used for?
questions.explanation: Attributes attach metadata to program elements such as classes, methods, properties, and assemblies.

questions.question: Which attribute can indicate that a method should no longer be used?
questions.explanation: ObsoleteAttribute marks a program element as obsolete and can produce a compiler warning or error.

questions.question: What does the true argument indicate in this declaration?
questions.code:
[Obsolete("Use NewMethod instead.", true)]
static void OldMethod() { }

options.text: Using OldMethod produces a compile-time error

questions.explanation: The second Obsolete argument specifies whether use of the obsolete member should generate a compiler error.

questions.question: Which namespace contains ConditionalAttribute?
questions.explanation: ConditionalAttribute is defined in the System.Diagnostics namespace.

questions.question: If the DEBUG symbol is not defined, what happens to calls to this method?

options.text: Calls to the method are omitted by the compiler
The method always throws an exception

questions.explanation: ConditionalAttribute controls whether calls to the method are included based on a compilation symbol. The method itself is not automatically deleted.

questions.question: What is the purpose of AttributeUsage when defining a custom attribute?

options.text: To specify which program elements can use the attribute and whether it can be inherited or repeated
To convert the attribute into a string

questions.explanation: AttributeUsage configures valid targets and options such as AllowMultiple and Inherited.

questions.question: Which namespace provides many of the core Reflection types?
questions.explanation: System.Reflection contains types used to inspect assemblies, types, methods, and other metadata.

questions.question: What does typeof(Student) return?

options.text: The name of the current method
A string containing the student's name

questions.explanation: typeof obtains type information for a type known at compile time.

questions.question: What is the difference between typeof(Student) and student.GetType()?

options.text: typeof requires an instance, while GetType does not
typeof obtains information from a type name at compile time, while GetType obtains the runtime type of an instance

questions.explanation: typeof refers to a known type, whereas GetType is called on an existing object to determine its runtime type.

questions.question: Which Reflection method retrieves method information from a Type?
questions.explanation: GetMethods retrieves MethodInfo objects describing methods available on a type, subject to the selected binding flags.

questions.question: What does Type.GetInterfaces() return?

options.text: A list of strings representing all fields
An array of Type objects representing implemented interfaces
A new instance of every interface
A list of method return values

questions.explanation: GetInterfaces returns Type objects representing the interfaces implemented or inherited by the type.

questions.question: What is the main problem with this code?
questions.code:
Type type = typeof(Student);
object instance = Activator.CreateInstance(type);

options.text: Activator.CreateInstance can fail if Student has no suitable accessible constructor or cannot be instantiated
typeof cannot be used with classes
object cannot store a reference to an instance

questions.explanation: Reflection-based instance creation depends on the type being instantiable and having a suitable constructor. Runtime exceptions are possible.

questions.question: How can Reflection be used to inspect a custom attribute applied to a class?

options.text: Use Reflection APIs such as GetCustomAttributes

questions.explanation: Reflection provides APIs for retrieving attribute metadata from types and members.

questions.question: What does the following custom attribute declaration allow?

options.text: The attribute can be applied to classes and stores a supplied name
The attribute can only be applied to local variables
The attribute automatically creates a course database
The attribute makes every class abstract

questions.explanation: AttributeTargets.Class restricts its use to classes, and the constructor stores the supplied name in the Name property.

questions.question: Which statement about Reflection is correct?

options.text: Reflection can inspect metadata about types and members at runtime

questions.explanation: Reflection enables runtime inspection of type metadata, members, and attributes.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between attributes and Reflection?

options.text: Attributes store metadata, and Reflection can inspect that metadata
Attributes and Reflection are identical concepts
Reflection is required to compile every C# method
Attributes can only be applied to strings

questions.explanation: Attributes attach metadata to program elements, and Reflection can retrieve and examine it.
